q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: WITH NODUPCUST AS ( SELECT DISTINCT CUSTOMER_ID ,PRODUCT_KEY FROM CUSTOMER ) SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM NODUPCUST GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID HAVING COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(*) AS PRODCOUNT FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: WITH NODUPCUST AS ( SELECT DISTINCT CUSTOMER_ID ,PRODUCT_KEY FROM CUSTOMER ) SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM NODUPCUST GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID HAVING COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(*) AS PRODCOUNT FROM PRODUCT)
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 1);
explanation: Q1 checks if the number of distinct products purchased by any customer is equal to the total number of distinct products in the database. Q2 checks if any customer has purchased all distinct products in the database. These are different conditions.
counterexample_dsp: A database with 2 products and 3 customers, where each customer has purchased a different product, triggers the difference.
